answer: A harbor admits only ships with a logged voyage; likewise, an agent economy can require each identity to earn standing through a probationary season of verifiable useful work before it may vote or claim rewards. Newcomers graze in a shared meadow of small audited tasks - labeling, verifying, routing - with earnings escrowed until a clean record accrues. That history becomes a relic no identity can cheaply re-mint: misbehavior burns escrow and reputation together. An attacker wanting ten thousand Sybils must pay ten thousand probationary seasons, while one honest agent pays it once.
